purpose: Additional comparative glossary and textual witnesses for the Nihāyat al-Ḥikma reader. Does not modify the authorial Arabic or the translation.

glossary.definition: The intellect in actuality as possessing intelligible contents, distinguished from initial receptivity or mere potentiality.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Dependence of a cause upon its own effect through a reciprocal causal sequence, not merely reciprocal logical implication.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Quiddity considered excluding an accompanying determination; central to certain discussions of genus, differentia, and form.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Quiddity considered together with a positive determination, such as humanity with the features of an individual.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The opposition of a proposition and its negation under the same respect, without an intermediate truth value in the classical account.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Opposition between contrary positive characteristics within one field; unlike contradiction, contraries may admit an intermediate.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The substantial form by which a material composite has three-dimensional extension in the author's analysis.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Opposition between correlative terms such as parent/child or above/below, where the meaning of each includes reference to the other.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Specification or determination of an existent. In discussions of existence, determination by degree must be distinguished from determination by a quiddity.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The essential determination distinguishing a species within a genus; distinguish this from a proprium that merely accompanies it.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The determination of one item as other than another; what grounds the distinction depends on whether the discussion concerns concepts, quiddities, or concrete existents.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: That which brings an effect into existence, with distinctions between complete and incomplete or preparatory forms of agency.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: A context-sensitive term for a thing's being established or obtaining. It must not automatically be identified with external existence in debates about non-existent things.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: An existent whose being, while actualising its own nature, also removes a privation from another, such as an accidental quality informing a subject.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Existence that actualises its own essence without thereby constituting the accidental perfection of a different subject; not identical to necessary existence.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Existence outside the mind, where a thing's characteristic external effects obtain, contrasted with the existence of its intelligible form in cognition.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The end for whose sake an operation is undertaken or made intelligible; not restricted to conscious intention in the author's account.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The first separate intellectual effect in the emanative hierarchy of the author's philosophical account; not to be identified uncritically with the Necessary Existent.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The determining substantial principle through which a material thing is the kind of thing that it is.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: An essential universal shared by different species. A genus alone does not constitute a full essential definition.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: An ontological level of imaginal forms described as distinct both from gross matter and from purely intellectual existence.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Existence intelligible as a subject of predication on its own, in contrast to a linking existence; independence of signification is not unrestricted causal independence.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The actuality whereby something is this individual rather than another. Tabāṭabāʾī connects individuation ultimately with existence, not a mere aggregation of universal predicates.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: An unending sequence; its impossibility in the relevant demonstration concerns an existentially ordered chain of causes, not every infinite series.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: What is grasped by intellect under an intelligible form; in intellectual self-presence, knower and intelligible are discussed as united.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: A quiddity, considered in itself, does not require either its existence or its non-existence; this is not the same as physical dispositional potential.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The receptive material principle of a composite substance; not identical with the agent that imparts actuality.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The nature considered as a common essence without the mind's extra consideration of its universality as a logical predicate.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Existence considered necessary rather than merely possible. The author sharply distinguishes necessity through another from intrinsic necessity.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Necessity following upon a sufficient cause, as distinct from necessary existence through the thing's own reality.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: A real capacity for an actuality, especially in the analysis of temporal coming-to-be; distinguish from merely conceivable possibility.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The position opposed to the primacy of existence: quiddity, rather than existence, is taken as fundamental in external reality. It must not be confused with the trivial claim that things have quiddities.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The purely potential, indeterminate principle in material substance, not a free-standing physical stuff with its own actuality.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: An accidental category, including dispositions and qualities; not all uses of the ordinary word 'how' denote the technical category.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: A category concerned with divisible magnitude or number, not to be confused with the relational category of place or position.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The accidental category ordered toward another. Distinguish it from the existential dependency that constitutes the effect as related to its cause.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Necessity considered in relation to another existent, particularly where correlatives imply one another, not a separate sufficient cause.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The absence of motion in a subject capable of moving, rather than absolute immutability without regard to motion.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The disputed possibility that numerically the same thing, after wholly ceasing to exist, could return. This is different from survival or transformation.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: An immaterial principle in its essence but connected with the body in its operation; its precise status differs from a wholly separate intellect.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: A complete specific nature resulting from the appropriate essential determination of a genus.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Change in substantial existence itself, not merely in its quantity, quality, or spatial location; central to the Sadrāian framework.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Existence considered as a reality, not merely the common concept signified by the word 'existence'. The distinction is indispensable for interpreting gradation.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The status of being a thing; the author argues that genuine thingness is coextensive with existence, rejecting a positive intermediate status for non-existents.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The measure of motion in the author's analysis, linked to the successive renewal and division of material existence.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The unity ascribed to pure necessary existence: not numerical oneness that admits another member of the same order.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: A way of considering quiddity without stipulating either the presence or the absence of a further determination; variants of this consideration must be distinguished.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

sources.title: Nihāyat al-Ḥikma, vol. 2 — revised 1428 AH edition, editor ʿAbbās ʿAlī al-Zāriʿī al-Sabzawārī
sources.description: Secondary collation witness only (vol. 2, 336 pp., 4th edition). Its pagination and critical notes differ from the existing Qum 1417 transcription and are not the reader’s current page locators.

statusNote: Supplementary apparatus includes inherited later-editor notes and one NEW unresolved IX.9 internal-reference conjecture. Only documented text witnesses support 'attested' labels; no critical specialist certification is implied.

criticalNotes.text: At the argument distinguishing quiddity from existence, the Qum 1417 AH reading is «ولو كانت عين الوجود لم يجز أن تسلب عن نفسها». In the revised 1428 AH edition, al-Zāriʿī prints «ولو كانت عين الوجود لم يجز أن يسلب عنها» and states explicitly in footnote 1 that the former is found in the copies and that he regards the latter as correct. The main reader adopts the editor's grammatical correction and preserves the earlier copy reading in its passage note. No manuscript collation of this locus is independently claimed.
criticalNotes.source: Nihāyat al-Ḥikma, vol. 1 (revised 1428 AH), p. 18 n. 1; compare Qum 1417 AH p. 18, edited by ʿAbbās ʿAlī al-Zāriʿī al-Sabzawārī
criticalNotes.status: Explicit later editorial emendation checked against printed editorial note; manuscript attestation unverified
criticalNotes.originalReading: ولو كانت عين الوجود لم يجز أن تسلب عن نفسها
criticalNotes.adoptedReading: ولو كانت عين الوجود لم يجز أن يسلب عنها

criticalNotes.text: The 1428 AH editor's long note listing eight positions on the reality of existence (vol. 1, printed p. 34) groups ‘Tomas Akoims’ (Thomas Aquinas) with absolute equivocation between God and creatures. This attribution is inaccurate: Aquinas, Summa theologiae I, q. 13, a. 5, explicitly rejects both univocal and purely equivocal predication in favour of analogy. This correction concerns the later editor's note; it is not a criticism of an assertion in Tabatabai's authorial chapter. Primary reference: https://www.newadvent.org/summa/1013.htm.
criticalNotes.source: 1428 AH Zāriʿī ed., vol. 1 pp. 33–34; Aquinas ST I q13 a5
criticalNotes.status: Checked against the two cited printed/public primary texts

criticalNotes.text: In the corrected 1428 AH witness (vol. 1, printed p. 36) the short footnote on negating a limit is explicitly marked ‘منه رحمه الله’ (‘from the author’). It explains that, because limitation has the character of negation, denying limitation is a negation of negation and therefore affirms the pure actuality of existence. The attribution is authorial; the surrounding longer explanatory footnotes belong to the later editor.
criticalNotes.source: 1428 AH Zāriʿī ed., vol. 1, printed p. 36, note marked منه رحمه الله

criticalNotes.text: The 1428 AH editor's note on the differentiation of non-existents (vol. 1, printed p. 38) cites Naṣīr al-Dīn al-Ṭūsī's Kashf al-Murād (p. 43) and proposes reconciling the apparent disagreement by distinguishing absolute non-being from absences considered in relation to particular things. This reconciliation is a later editorial gloss, not an authorial assertion to be inserted into Tabāṭabāʾī's matn; its reading of Ṭūsī requires separate verification against Kashf al-Murād.
criticalNotes.source: 1428 AH Zāriʿī ed., vol. 1, printed p. 38, editorial note on Ṭūsī
criticalNotes.status: Secondary interpretation; primary Ṭūsī text not yet collated

criticalNotes.text: In the 1428 AH revised edition vol. 1 p. 52 n. 6, al-Zāriʿī says that all copies read «كان جوهرا أو عرضا موجودا في نفسه رابطا بالنظر إلى علّته» but deletes «موجودا في نفسه» as superfluous and, without the subsequent restriction ‘considered in itself’, misleading. The reading edition adopts the explicit editorial deletion in Arabic and English. The phrase from the 1417 AH base and the editor's rationale remain in the passage note; manuscript evidence for the omission has not been claimed.
criticalNotes.source: Nihāyat al-Ḥikma, edited 1428 AH vol. 1 p. 52 n. 6; prior 1417 AH Qum text, II.2
criticalNotes.status: Explicit editorial deletion from copies, checked against printed note; no manuscript attestation of omission
criticalNotes.originalReading: كان جوهرا أو عرضا موجودا في نفسه رابطا بالنظر إلى علّته
criticalNotes.adoptedReading: كان جوهرا أو عرضا رابطا بالنظر إلى علّته

criticalNotes.text: The 1417 AH reading has «عطف الصور الطبيعيّة» (plural), but the revised 1428 AH edition vol. 1 p. 158 n. 1 explicitly notes that the copies have the plural and prints «عطف الصورة الطبيعيّة» (singular), agreeing with the subsequent singular pronoun and adjective «وهي متأخّرة». The reader adopts the editor's correction, preserves the transmitted plural in a passage note, and does not claim a manuscript source for the singular.
criticalNotes.source: ʿAbbās ʿAlī al-Zāriʿī, 1428 AH revised edition, vol. 1 p. 158 n. 1; 1417 Qum, Stage VI.3
criticalNotes.status: Later editor's explicit emendation checked; transmitted plural preserved; manuscript attestation unverified

criticalNotes.text: In vol. 1 p. 209 nn. 3–4 the 1428 revised editor states that the copies give «كمالاتها الثانية» at the second occurrence and «يتميّز به» for the act of discriminating by knowledge. He prints «كمالاته الثانية» to refer the perfections to the human being and «يميّز به» so that the agent distinguishes by knowledge. The earlier «من كمالاتها الثانية» referring to the soul remains correct and was not altered. Two explicit editorial conjectures are accepted with earlier readings preserved in N-VI-15 apparatus.
criticalNotes.source: Nihāyat al-Ḥikma 1428 revised edition, vol. 1 p. 209 nn. 3–4; compare 1417 base
criticalNotes.status: Later-editor textual decisions; not manuscript-attested readings

criticalNotes.text: The 1417 base says «ينتزع من الموضوعين الواجدين للنسبة المتكرّرة المتلازمة وصفاً ناعتاً لهما». In vol. 1 p. 218 n. 4 the 1428 editor prints «ينتزع لكلّ من الموضوعين ... وصفاً ناعتاً له» and explicitly records the earlier copy reading. The correction changes the analysis from one common property attributed jointly to both relata to one relational predicate of each term, dependent on their reciprocal relation. Both Arabic and English were corrected; old wording remains in the authorial passage note. The nearby «لوقوعها» was already correct in the 1417 reader. In the same chapter (vol. 1 p. 218 n. 1) he also corrects «المضاف إلى الابن» to «المضاف إلى الأب», since the subject bearing sonship is related to a father. The reader adopts this correction in both Arabic and English and retains the prior wording as a documented copy reading.
criticalNotes.source: Nihāyat al-Ḥikma 1428 revised edition, vol. 1 p. 218 nn. 1 and 4; compare 1417 base
criticalNotes.status: Later-editor textual decision; manuscript attestation unverified
criticalNotes.originalReading: ينتزع من الموضوعين ... وصفاً ناعتاً لهما
criticalNotes.adoptedReading: ينتزع لكلّ من الموضوعين ... وصفاً ناعتاً له

criticalNotes.type: Unresolved internal cross-reference · not an attested emendation
criticalNotes.text: In Chapter IX.9, printed p. 265, the author contrasts (1) longitudinal substantial motion, where matter and the earlier form become the substrate of a later form, with (2) parallel succession, where an enduring matter receives mutually exclusive forms. The text nevertheless says «لا بطريق الخلع واللبس كما في القسم الأول، بل بطريق اللبس بعد اللبس»—'not by stripping off and putting on, as in the first kind, but by putting on after putting on'—inside its account of the FIRST (longitudinal) kind. In light of the immediately preceding distinction and the following 'first/second' conclusions, «القسم الثاني» is a plausible INTERNAL editorial conjecture for «القسم الأول». The 1417 AH printed-digital source itself reads «الأول». No independent 1404/1428 print or manuscript has been checked at this exact phrase in this review. We leave the copied Arabic and the working English unchanged, record the difficulty, and DO NOT treat the conjecture as witnessed or adopted. A future editor must report exact witness readings and any adopted before/after change.
criticalNotes.source: Ṭabāṭabāʾī, Nihāyat al-Ḥikma, Qum 1417 AH digitally transcribed print, p.265; witnessed reading at this stage ONLY in that base digital presentation; additional print collation outstanding
criticalNotes.status: unresolved internal textual inconsistency; conjecture not adopted; no independent witness attestation

sourceCriticalPolicy: Preserve authorial notes explicitly marked منه رحمه الله; distinguish later editor's explanatory notes; challenge historically questionable ascriptions by checking named scholars' own texts. These criticalNotes are distinct from the authorial Arabic and translation.
